newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Hong Kong subversion law unacceptable.
newsitem.headline: China says Hong Kong subversion law unacceptable.

text.p: China on Thursday slammed a subversion bill for Hong Kong as unacceptable, but stopped short of saying if it would be scrapped after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule in 1997.

Britain took steps this week to bring in a law on subversion ahead of Hong Kong's mid-1997 return, laying down legal markers defining the concepts of treason, sedition, subversion and secession in a bid to head off jailings of dissidents after Beijing takes over the colony.

"The Chinese side cannot accept such actions that exceed the limit of the British side's power and meddle in the affairs of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region," Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a news briefing.

"The British Hong Kong government is forcefully revising the existing crimes ordinance before 1997," Cui said, quoting a statement by the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office under the State Council, or cabinet.
"(This is) an infringement of the legislative power of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and a violation of the provisions of the Basic Law," Cui said.
The spokesman did not say if China would scrap the law after resuming sovereignty at midnight next June 30.
Pro-China politicians in Hong Kong have said the law will probably be erased and replaced after the Chinese takeover.
Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten, speaking in Tokyo on Wednesday, defended his government's move to introduce the bill and criticised Beijing for refusing to talk about the issue.
